pages.title: A07 · Bronze to silver cleaning
lede: Objectives (S3): clean nulls, standardize types, write new silver tables; add, drop, split, rename, filter.
Serverless runs American National Standards Institute (ANSI) SQL mode by default (as do Spark 4.0, Runtime 17.0+).

blocks.heading: 1. Trap: cast vs try_cast (ANSI mode on)
blocks.code:
bronze.select(F.col("amount").cast("decimal(10,2)")).show()   # [CAST_INVALID_INPUT] 'N/A' is malformed
typed = bronze.withColumn("amount", F.expr("try_cast(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2))"))   # N/A -> NULL
bad = bronze.filter(F.col("amount").isNotNull() & F.expr("try_cast(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2))").isNull())
bad.count()   # 1 (order 1002)
blocks.note: cast: one bad value fails the query. try_cast: NULL (impossible type pairs still error). Count the NULLs.

blocks.heading: 2. Traps: dropna and fillna
blocks.code:
bronze.dropna().count()                       # 0  how="any": every row has a null _rescued_data
bronze.dropna(subset=["order_id"]).count()    # 5  how="all" -> 6, thresh=n keeps n+ non-nulls
bronze.fillna(0)                              # string customer_name still NULL (type mismatch ignored)
bronze.fillna({"customer_name": "unknown"})   # use a dict
blocks.note: dropna() with no subset can empty a table. fillna only fills columns of the value's type.

blocks.heading: 3. The full bronze to silver chain
blocks.code:
silver = (bronze
  .dropna(subset=["order_id"])                                   # nulls: drop rows
  .withColumn("order_id", F.col("order_id").cast("int"))
  .withColumn("amount", F.expr("try_cast(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2))"))   # types
  .withColumn("order_date", F.to_date("order_date", "yyyy-MM-dd"))
  .withColumn("customer_name", F.trim("customer_name"))
  .fillna({"customer_name": "unknown"})                          # nulls: fill
  .withColumn("city", F.split("city_state", ", ").getItem(0))     # split, add
  .withColumn("state", F.split("city_state", ", ").getItem(1))
  .drop("city_state", "_rescued_data")                           # drop
  .withColumnRenamed("customer_name", "customer")                # rename
  .filter(F.col("amount").isNotNull()))                          # filter
silver.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("silver_orders")      # 6 bronze -> 3 silver: 1001, 1003, 1006
blocks.note: withColumn adds or replaces. split takes a regex. ANSI: getItem past the end fails, get() returns NULL.

pages.title: SQL version, rejected rows, snippet, checklist

blocks.heading: 4. The same silver table in SQL: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS)
blocks.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_orders AS
SELECT CAST(order_id AS INT) AS order_id, coalesce(trim(customer_name), 'unknown') AS customer,
       try_cast(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS amount, to_date(order_date) AS order_date,
       split(city_state, ', ')[0] AS city, split(city_state, ', ')[1] AS state
FROM bronze_orders WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL AND try_cast(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2)) IS NOT NULL;
blocks.note: coalesce = fillna; leaving a column out of the SELECT = drop. Same 3 rows.

blocks.heading: 5. On the job: count what you rejected
blocks.code:
reason = (F.when(F.col("order_id").isNull(), "no order_id").when(F.col("amount").isNull(), "no amount")
  .when(F.expr("try_cast(amount AS DECIMAL(10,2))").isNull(), "bad amount"))
rejected = bronze.withColumn("reason", reason).filter(F.col("reason").isNotNull())   # groupBy: 1 each
print(bronze.count(), silver.count(), rejected.count())   # 6 3 3  -> save as orders_rejected

blocks.heading: 6. Reusable snippet: try_cast and count
blocks.code:
def try_cast_count(df, col, to="DECIMAL(10,2)"):
    typed = F.expr(f"try_cast({col} AS {to})")
    bad = df.filter(F.col(col).isNotNull() & typed.isNull())
    print(f"{col}: {bad.count()} bad value(s)")
    return df.withColumn(col, typed), bad

blocks.heading: 7. Bronze to silver checklist
blocks.text: 1) Read bronze, write a NEW silver table. 2) Required columns only: dropna(subset=[...]). 3) try_cast, then count the NULLs it made. 4) Fill with a dict, not fillna(0). 5) Check columns after drop / withColumnRenamed (missing columns are ignored). 6) Reconcile: bronze = silver + rejected. Memory trick: cast fails loud. try_cast fails quiet. A quiet NULL still needs a count.
